title: Unlocking the complex interplay between epigenetics and epitranscriptomics in neuropsychiatric disorders
title_zh: 揭示表观遗传学与表转录组学在神经精神疾病中的复杂相互作用
abstract: Abstract Epigenetic and epitranscriptomic mechanisms work together to control gene expression, which is essential for brain development, synaptic plasticity, and the risk of neuropsychiatric disorders. Traditional epigenetic processes, such as DNA methylation and histone modifications, alter chromatin structure to regulate gene accessibility. On the other hand, epitranscriptomic marks such as N6-methyladenosine (m6A) affect RNA metabolism after transcription. Studies in both neural and non-neural systems show that these layers of regulation interact in both directions and together shape gene expression. This review looks at how m6A-modified non-coding RNAs, including chromosome-associated regulatory RNAs (carRNAs), enhancer RNAs (eRNAs), microRNAs, and circular RNAs, work with chromatin to influence genome function, including chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and the overall structure of the genome. It also covers recent discoveries about how eRNAs form R-loops, how m6A affects RNA stability, and how these processes are involved in neuronal signaling and plasticity. Many of these findings come from studies outside the nervous system and need more research in neuropsychiatric disease models. By bringing together established knowledge and new ideas, this review suggests that the interaction between epigenetic and epitranscriptomic mechanisms is a key factor in determining risk and resilience for neuropsychiatric disorders, and offers new directions for future research and therapy development.
abstract_zh: 摘要：表观遗传与表转录组机制共同调控基因表达，这对大脑发育、突触可塑性以及神经精神疾病的风险至关重要。传统的表观遗传过程，如 DNA 甲基化和组蛋白修饰，通过改变染色质结构来调节基因可及性。相反，表转录组标记如 N6‑甲基腺苷（m6A）则影响转录后 RNA 的代谢。神经和非神经系统的研究均表明，这些调控层面相互作用、相互影响，共同塑造基因表达。本综述探讨了 m6A 修饰的非编码 RNA（包括染色体相关调控 RNA（carRNAs）、增强子 RNA（eRNAs）、microRNA 和环状 RNA）如何与染色质协同作用，影响基因组功能，包括染色质可及性、组蛋白修饰以及基因组整体结构。文中还讨论了 eRNAs 形成 R‑loop、m6A 对 RNA 稳定性的影响以及这些过程在神经信号传导和可塑性中的作用等最新发现。许多结论来自神经系统外的研究，仍需在神经精神疾病模型中进一步验证。通过整合既有知识与新见解，本文认为表观遗传与表转录组机制的相互作用是决定神经精神疾病风险与韧性的关键因素，并为未来研究与治疗开发提供了新方向。
